stem.en: Magnesium ribbon burns in carbon dioxide. It keeps burning, and black carbon specks appear. Which is true?

text.en: Magnesium is oxidised, losing electrons, and the carbon in carbon dioxide is reduced, gaining them. Oxygen changes partners but is not "the oxidiser" here.
Nothing is oxidised, because carbon dioxide has no free oxygen.

feedback.en: Magnesium loses electrons, so it is oxidised. What takes them is the carbon, which ends up as black carbon.

text.en: Magnesium is reduced, because it takes the oxygen off the carbon dioxide.

feedback.en: Taking oxygen is not the definition any more. Magnesium loses electrons, and losing is oxidation.
The carbon gains electrons and comes out as carbon. Gaining is reduction.

explanation.en: Follow the electrons, not the oxygen. Magnesium's outer electrons end up on the carbon. Whoever loses is oxidised, whoever gains is reduced.
